title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the essential corridors and micro-districts surrounding Azusa Pacific University, from the student-favorite eateries on Alosta Avenue to the transit hubs connecting campus to Greater Los Angeles.

cards.title: The 'South Campus' Hub
cards.subtitle: Alosta Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the Chick-fil-A at 950 E Alosta Ave, famously nicknamed 'South Campus' by APU students who use Cougar Bucks here for meals and study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A commercial center on Alosta Avenue serving as a primary off-campus social and dining hub for the APU community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chick-fil-A in Azusa is a popular off-campus spot for APU students, nicknamed 'South Campus' and accepting Cougar Bucks.
cards.source_title: Great Places to Do Homework in the Azusa Community
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; Chick-fil-A hours typically 6:30 AM to 10:00 PM, closed Sundays.

cards.title: The Gateway to LA
cards.subtitle: Citrus Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Catch the Metro A Line (formerly Gold Line) at this terminal station on Citrus Avenue for direct light rail access to Pasadena and Downtown Los Angeles.
cards.short_summary: The northern terminus of the Metro A Line, providing essential regional transit for APU commuters and weekend travelers.
cards.evidence_claim: The APU/Citrus College Station is located on Citrus Avenue and serves as the final stop on the line connecting Azusa to Los Angeles.
cards.source_title: Commuter Services and Student Resources | APU
cards.access_notes: Public transit station; trains run daily from early morning until approximately midnight.

cards.title: The Repurposed Study House
cards.subtitle: Foothill Boulevard Corridor
cards.notes: Study in a cozy, home-like atmosphere at this repurposed house on Foothill Blvd, known for student-friendly hours until midnight.
cards.short_summary: A popular student coffee house located in a converted residence along historic Route 66.
cards.evidence_claim: Mantra Coffee is a repurposed house in Azusa providing student-friendly hours from 7 a.m. to midnight.
cards.source_title: Great Places to Do Homework in the Azusa Community
cards.access_notes: Open daily until midnight, making it a key late-night study destination.

cards.title: The Route 66 Landmark
cards.subtitle: Azusa Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the 1928 Mission-style City Hall, a National Historic Landmark that anchors the downtown district north of Foothill Blvd.
cards.short_summary: The historic heart of Azusa's civic life, featuring iconic architecture and the Route 66 Centennial Monument.
cards.evidence_claim: Azusa City Hall, completed in 1928, is recognized as the city's only National Historic Landmark along Route 66.
cards.source_title: Azusa, CA - Route 66 Centennial Monument Project
cards.access_notes: Public grounds accessible daily; building hours vary by department.

cards.title: The Glendora Village Escape
cards.subtitle: Glendora Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Drive just east of campus to Glendora Avenue for this popular pastry and coffee spot, a frequent alternative to on-campus libraries.
cards.short_summary: A nearby coffee shop in the Glendora Village district favored by APU students for its quiet atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: Classic Coffee on Glendora Avenue is a short drive from APU and a popular spot for students to do homework.
cards.source_title: Great Places to Do Homework in the Azusa Community
cards.access_notes: Open daily; check seasonal hours for early morning or late evening study sessions.

cards.title: The Student Housing Strip
cards.subtitle: Alosta Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk past this major residential complex at 801 E Alosta Ave, formerly known as University Village, which houses many APU upperclassmen.
cards.short_summary: A large apartment community adjacent to East Campus that serves as a primary off-campus residence for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The apartments at 801 East Alosta Avenue, formerly University Village, are now called Citrus Place.
cards.source_title: Azusa Pacific University apartments trade hands for $91.8M
cards.access_notes: Private residential complex; sidewalk access along Alosta Avenue is public.

cards.title: The Quiet Productivity Nook
cards.subtitle: Foothill Boulevard Corridor
cards.notes: Find a quiet table at this lesser-known coffee shop on Foothill Blvd, offering a full lunch menu and 12-hour daily availability.
cards.short_summary: A tranquil coffee and lunch spot located near the East Campus commercial area.
cards.evidence_claim: aDosage Coffee provides a quiet atmosphere for productivity and is open 12 hours a day for most of the week.
cards.source_title: Great Places to Do Homework in the Azusa Community
cards.access_notes: Open daily; typically 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM.

cards.title: The Civic Transit Link
cards.subtitle: Azusa Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Use this station to access the Azusa Intermodal Transit Center, where students can transfer between the A Line and Foothill Transit buses.
cards.short_summary: A central transit hub in downtown Azusa connecting the Metro rail system with local bus routes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Azusa Intermodal Transit Center allows for transfers to Foothill Transit Line 187, serving various local destinations.
cards.access_notes: Public transit facility; parking available via Metro's Preferred Parking Program.

cards.title: The Mother Road Tribute
cards.subtitle: Foothill Boulevard Corridor
cards.notes: Stop by the corner of Foothill and Alameda to see the 'Greetings from Azusa' mural, celebrating the city's identity as a Route 66 gateway.
cards.short_summary: A large-scale public mural and monument commemorating Azusa's history on the historic Mother Road.
cards.evidence_claim: A Route 66 mural and Centennial Monument are located at the corner of Foothill Blvd and Alameda, adjacent to City Hall.
cards.source_title: Azusa, CA - Route 66 Centennial Monument Project
cards.access_notes: Public art installation visible from the sidewalk 24/7.

cards.title: The Nature Study Spot
cards.subtitle: Citrus Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk north on Citrus Avenue to reach this 11-acre park, offering walking trails and a peaceful alternative to campus lawns for studying.
cards.short_summary: A quiet municipal park north of campus used by students for recreation and outdoor study.
cards.evidence_claim: Northside Park is a great spot for students to enjoy walking trails and a peaceful atmosphere for study sessions.
cards.source_title: Free and Affordable Activities for College Students at APU
cards.access_notes: Public park; open daily from dawn to dusk.
